title: Point-system power law and normalized inverse-image limit compositor
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and on the small pro-etale site set $B_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\widehat R_s=\lim_nB_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_s$ be the abelian category of strict $B_n$-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, with its ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $U_s$ for levelwise restriction to $\widehat R_s$-module towers and $\mathcal L_s=R\lim U_s$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put $F_r=(h^r)^{-1}$ on module complexes with scalars transported through the canonical coefficient isomorphisms, and $G_r$ for its levelwise functor on systems [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Read the finite levels through $j_{r,M}:F_rM\to(h^r)^*M$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, of part (a) of the latter definition. Let $\Gamma_\bullet$ be restriction of scalars followed by exact sections levelwise, retaining all transitions [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

Let $u_{r,M}$ and $I_{r,C}$ be the restriction/insertion/tensor-unit maps of [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent]. Let $d_m:F_1F_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{m+1}$ be the canonical site inverse-image compositor, and let $t_m:G_1G_m\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{m+1}$ be its whole-system version, read through $j_r$; at finite tensor levels its inverse is the canonical pullback-composition map of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. For every $m\geq1$ and every strict system complex $M$ one has the equality of chain maps of entire $R$-module towers
$$u_{m+1,M}=\Gamma_\bullet(t_{m,M})\circ u_{1,G_mM}\circ u_{m,M}.$$
In the site-reindexing model its restriction component is the composite of restriction along $h^m$ with restriction along $h$, equal to restriction along $h^m\circ h=h^{m+1}$; its tensor component under $t_m$ sends $(x\otimes1)\otimes1$ to $x\otimes1$. These identities hold in every degree with the actual quotient-linear transitions. After localization,
$$I_{m+1,C}=\Gamma_\bullet(t_{m,C})\circ I_{1,G_mC}\circ I_{m,C}$$
for all $C\in D(\mathscr S_s)$.

For such $C$ put $N=\mathcal L_sC$. Specify $a_{r,C}:F_rN\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_sG_rC$ by the canonical product comparison on BOTH summands of $H(U_sM)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ for a strict representative $M$, through the normalized total-limit identification [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison, lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Thus a product projection of $a$ is inverse image applied to the corresponding projection, and its off-diagonal components vanish. No constructibility assumption on $N$ is made. The following is an identity of the specified natural derived maps:
$$a_{m+1,C}\circ d_{m,N}=\mathcal L_s(t_{m,C})\circ a_{1,G_mC}\circ F_1(a_{m,C}):F_1F_mN\longrightarrow\mathcal L_sG_{m+1}C.$$
On each shifted and unshifted product summand this is equality of the canonical product maps: for every $n$ their $n$th projection is the same twice-reindexed projection, with the inserted tensor units multiplied by $t_m$. This specifies whole-cone compositor coherence, not a claim that derived evaluations detect equality of morphisms.

proof.text: First check the coefficient identifications in the compositor. Apply [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition] with the two maps $h$ and $h^m$ and with the finite ring $A_n$. It gives $c_{m+1,n}d_{m,B_n}=c_{1,n}F_1(c_{m,n})$. The finite identifications commute with coefficient reduction by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](3). For completed coefficients, compose the analogous asserted equality with every $\pi_n$ and use $\pi_nc_{r,\widehat R}=c_{r,n}F_r(\pi_n)$ from [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Each composite is the finite equality just proved, so the universal property of the coefficient limit proves the completed equality too. Consequently the reindexing identification $F_1F_m=F_{m+1}$ respects transported module actions and restriction of scalars. Here and below finite module pullbacks are read through the specified $j_r$, never identified with inverse image by an arbitrary isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 03CB (lemma-composition-morphisms-sites), 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf); coefficient-limit extension of the constant-section calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-point-sheaf-insertion-calculus] with $A=A_n$ to each sheaf $M_n^i$. Its normalized reindexing isomorphism identifies the insertion recipe of [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent] with restriction along $h^r$. Successive restrictions give $\operatorname{res}_h\operatorname{res}_{h^m}=\operatorname{res}_{h^m\circ h}=\operatorname{res}_{h^{m+1}}$. In the tensor presentation, the inverse of the canonical pullback-composition isomorphism sends $(x\otimes1)\otimes1$ to $x\otimes1$, as in that insertion-calculus identity. Thus $u_{m+1,n}^i=\Gamma(t_{m,M_n^i})u_{1,G_mM_n^i}u_{m,n}^i$. The identification is with the $t_m$ in the statement: [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] specifies the canonical termwise pullback compositor, and the pullbacks along isomorphisms here are exact, as in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](a).

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: compatibility with composition; explicit point restriction and tensor-unit calculation

proof.text: This is equality of strict tower chain maps. Indeed [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent] supplies the original quotient-linear transition squares and differential commutation. On the transition $v_n$, either insertion path sends $(x\otimes1)\otimes1$ to $v_n(x)\otimes\rho_n(1)=v_n(x)\otimes1$; Step 1 supplies its completed scalar compatibility. The compositor commutes with $v_n$ and $d^i$ by its naturality. Equality of all the components in Step 2 is therefore equality in the category of complexes of strict $R$-module towers. Localize this equality. By the same descent node, the localized $u_r$ is precisely $I_r$, and the exact functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Since localization preserves composition, it gives $I_{m+1,C}=\Gamma_\bullet(t_{m,C})I_{1,G_mC}I_{m,C}$ on the ordinary derived SYSTEM category.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers, retaining transitions before localization

proof.text: Put $X=U_sM$ for a strict representative $M$ of $C$, and identify $U_sG_rM$ with $F_rX$ through the coefficient maps checked in Step 1. By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] countable products of completed-module sheaves are sectionwise and exact. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] the reindexing functor is exact and preserves products; transporting scalars through a ring isomorphism changes no underlying kernel, cokernel or product, as specified in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Thus [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] applies to $F_r$ on the entire unbounded module category. Write $\theta_X:R\lim X\xrightarrow{\sim}H(X)$ for its normalized Roos coordinates, $\phi_{r,X}:F_rP_X\to P_{F_rX}$ for the canonical product map and $\kappa_{r,X}:F_rH(X)\to H(F_rX)$ for that map on both coordinates. The specified comparison is $a_{r,C}=\theta_{F_rX}^{-1}\kappa_{r,X}F_r(\theta_X)$. Naturality of these identifications and diagonal maps is supplied by [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] and [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-roos-chain-maps].

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof; normalized exact-product comparison specified by the cited nodes

proof.text:
Let $T=U_st_{m,M}:F_1F_mX\to F_{m+1}X$ in the identifications of Step 4. It is the degreewise compositor, and let $P(T)$ be its product map. In every degree the product maps satisfy
$$\phi_{m+1,X}d_{m,P_X}=P(T)\phi_{1,F_mX}F_1(\phi_{m,X}).$$
To verify this, compose the left side with the $n$th product projection. Its value is $F_{m+1}(\mathrm{pr}_n)d_{m,P_X}=T_nF_1F_m(\mathrm{pr}_n)$ by naturality of $d_m$. On the right the two defining product-projection equations give $T_nF_1(F_m(\mathrm{pr}_n))$, the same map. Product uniqueness proves the equality. The projection equations used here are exactly those of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-roos-chain-maps]. In the reindexing model both are the twice-reindexed projection; on finite tensor presentations Step 2 multiplies the two inserted units. The calculation is at the level of products of complexes, before derived localization.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers; product-projection calculation for the canonical inverse-image comparison

proof.text:
Use the signed coordinates of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]: $H(X)^i=P_X^i\oplus P_X^{i-1}$ and $D(x,y)=(dx,(1-s_X)x-dy)$. The functorial cone maps of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] send a strict tower map $f$ to the diagonal map with entries $P(f)$. Since $T$ commutes with the actual transitions, $P(T)s_{F_1F_mX}=s_{F_{m+1}X}P(T)$; this follows by composing with $\mathrm{pr}_n$ and using $T_nv_n=v'_nT_{n+1}$. The same projection calculation shows the product comparisons commute with the shifts $s$. They therefore commute with $1-s$, and the displayed differential verifies they are cone chain maps. Step 5 applied in degrees $i$ and $i-1$ proves
$$\kappa_{m+1,X}d_{m,H(X)}=H(T)\kappa_{1,F_mX}F_1(\kappa_{m,X}).$$
Both sides have the same diagonal entries, and both off-diagonal entries are zero. This proves equality on the entire cone, including its shifted coordinate.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers; the same product calculation on both signed Roos coordinates

proof.text:
Finally conjugate Step 6 by the specified normalized Roos identifications of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Naturality of $d_m$ gives $F_{m+1}(\theta_X)d_{m,R\lim X}=d_{m,H(X)}F_1F_m(\theta_X)$. Substituting the formula for $a$ from Step 4 into the left side of the required identity, Step 6 gives
$$\theta_{F_{m+1}X}^{-1}H(T)\kappa_{1,F_mX}F_1(\kappa_{m,X})F_1F_m(\theta_X).$$
On the right, naturality of $\theta$ from [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] gives $\mathcal L_s(t_m)=\theta_{F_{m+1}X}^{-1}H(T)\theta_{F_1F_mX}$. Substitution cancels $\theta_{F_1F_mX}\theta_{F_1F_mX}^{-1}$ and $F_1(\theta_{F_mX})F_1(\theta_{F_mX}^{-1})$, giving exactly the same displayed expression. This is the desired compositor identity. All these cone constructions descend naturally by the cited Roos comparison, so the calculation holds for every $C$ and naturally for its derived morphisms. Only strict product and cone equalities were localized; no faithfulness of derived evaluations or constructibility of $\mathcal L_sC$ was used.
